messages:
incident-bot: Paging: multiple driver resets observed on gpu-cluster-prod-3 (Xid=13/31) across nodes 3,4,7. ECC correctable counters spiking. Auto-alert triggered at 2026-03-15T07:40:32Z. Severity: SEV-2.
maya: saw the alert, grabbing the on-call.
jon: I'm oncall, taking this. Starting quick triage — is there any customer-facing impact reported yet?
incident-bot: No active customer bridges open. Some inference jobs retried; autoscaler reported 12 evicted pods in the last 5m (pods in ns=redwood-inference).
kevin: I can confirm repeated nv-host-engine logs on node gpu-3: `NVRM: Xid (13): PID 2314 GPU at 00000000:03:00.0` and container OOMs following.
jon: copying logs into thread.
jon: ```
Mar 15 07:38:59 gpu-3 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13) at 0x12345
Mar 15 07:39:01 gpu-3 kubelet: Pod redwood-inference/pod-abc123: container "runtime" exited with status 137 (OOMKilled)
Mar 15 07:39:02 gpu-3 systemd: nvidia-fabric: reset request
```
maya: thanks. Let's assess blast radius: which customer routes are pinned to Dedicated pools that hit these nodes?
ops_lead: Dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-1` has 3 hosts across nodes gpu-3 and gpu-4. Traffic shift to other regions was disabled for this pool.
jon: tagging @ops_lead for immediate cordon suggestion.
ops_lead: cordoning gpu-3 and gpu-4 now to stop new pods scheduling (running `kubectl cordon gpu-3`).
kevin: suggest we scale down non-critical batches and drain inference nodes gracefully to avoid further OOM churn.
sre-oncall: initiating drain: `kubectl drain gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
jon: while draining, I'm going to check GPU ECC telemetry. kevin can you dump `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.volatile.uncorrected,duty_cycle`?
kevin: output: ```
GPU 0: ecc.correctable: 128 -> 1024 in last 10m
GPU 1: ecc.correctable: 0 -> 16
GPU 2: ecc.correctable: 4 -> 512
```
jon: big spike on GPU0/GPU2, matches node-level resets. Not typical thermal pattern — temps are 58-72C.
maya: any quick mitigation that doesn't require reboots?
kevin: we can try fencing the offending GPU via MIG or isolating the device to the kernel before full host restart. I'll attempt device reset via `nvidia-persistenced` and `echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:03:00.0/reset` on a trial node (with low load).
jon: be careful — force reset can drop all running containers. We should pick one non-critical node for test.
sre-oncall: selected gpu-7 (low load). Proceeding.
kevin: applied soft reset, device came back but Xid continued to appear after ~4 minutes. Looks like resets only temporarily mask the issue.
jon: ok, we need escalation plan. If soft resets fail, we should do full host reboot in a rolling fashion and route customers accordingly.
maya: opening a customer bridge proactively. customer-bridge-bot: Customer Bridge created for incident 2498765432. Bridge URL: https://bridge.internal/redwood/2498765432 (ops only).
jon: documenting impact: some short-lived 5xx errors for customers using Dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-1` and increased latency for host-pinned jobs. Autoscaler made retry storms for ephemeral jobs, causing higher control-plane load. No confirmed data loss.
ops_lead: start failover for pinned routes: switching routing policy to fallback-models and enabling cross-region spill to us-west-2 for new requests. Rolling this change now.
kevin: rolling restart sequence prepared: gpu-7 -> gpu-3 -> gpu-4 -> gpu-2. Each host reboot followed by smoke tests: `nvidia-smi`, health checks, and short inference load.
jon: assign owners for restarts and customer communication. kevin owns restarts, maya on customer comms, jon monitoring.
maya: posting to affected customers with interim note: "We are investigating GPU driver resets impacting some Dedicated hosts in eu region; we are performing rolling mitigation and will follow up with timeline. No data loss expected"
kevin: performing first host reboot on gpu-7 now. Reboot command: `ssh ops@gpu-7 sudo reboot`
jon: monitoring logs and job reschedules. If resets stop after first two reboots, we'll consider rolling remainder.
kevin: after reboot, nv-host logs show stable behavior for 18m so far; ECC correctable counters not spiking.
jon: good sign. Continue with next reboot.
sre-oncall: gpu-3 restart in progress; draining completed beforehand.
kevin: gpu-3 came back but one container in ns=redwood-inference still got OOMKilled after reschedule — may need to tweak K8s eviction thresholds for the pool to prevent repeated retries.
jon: temporary fix: increase pod eviction grace and add backoff on retries for batch jobs. ops_lead, can you push the k8s patch to the pool config?
ops_lead: patch applied: `evictionGraceSeconds=120`, restartBackoff=60s for batch jobs in dedicated pools.
maya: customer-bridge-bot: Sent update to customers at 07:59Z.
jon: post-mortem notes to capture: root cause hypothesis = hardware instability causing GPU driver resets (Xid 13/31) amplified by autoscaler retry/backoff config leading to OOM churn; corrective actions = rolling host reboots, cordon/drain policy, increase eviction/backoff, enable cross-region spill, and open ticket with hardware vendor for ECC trend.
kevin: I'll open vendor ticket with full nv-host logs and ECC counters attached.
maya: handing off to night oncall. Summary: mitigations applied, customer comm in place, vendor ticket opened, follow-ups: vendor RMA if hardware confirmed, permanent routing policy for Dedicated failover, revisit autoscaler thresholds.
jon: taking ack. Marking incident as monitoring. If we see new Xid > 5 events in 30m escalate back to paging.
incident-bot: Incident 2498765432 status changed to MONITORING at 2026-03-15T08:03:20Z.
customer-bridge-bot: Final update posted to customers at 08:10Z: "Rolling mitigations complete; traffic restored with fallback; working with vendor to determine root cause; next update in 6h or earlier if new issues."
maya: handing off fully to night shift @sre-oncall.
sre-oncall: acknowledged, will monitor ECC counters and Xid rate. If trend rises, will escalate and reopen bridge.
jon: thanks team. End of thread."
